record_body:
Account summary
- Helio Ledger (EU fintech) building an internal “Ops Copilot” used by L2/L3 support + risk teams. Heavy sensitivity to tail latency (agent UX) and change-management (weekly model/version updates).
- Strong preference for Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + isolation) with EU-only data processing.

Primary requirements (from eval scoping)
- Workload mix:
  - Chat (support agent) w/ streaming
  - Summarization (case notes, call transcripts)
  - Doc-search (embeddings + rerank)
- Latency SLOs (customer-stated):
  - Chat: p95 TTFT < 500ms, p95 end-to-end < 2.5s for typical prompts (1–2k input tokens, ~250–400 output)
  - Summarization: p95 < 6s (non-streaming)
  - Error SLO: < 0.2% 5xx (monthly), wants route-level visibility
- Throughput expectations:
  - Peak: 150–250 concurrent chats during business hours; spikes during incident response
  - Batch jobs (summarization): up to 20k docs/night; cost sensitivity moderate but needs predictable window
- Change-management:
  - Wants canary + A/B support; “no surprise regressions” is key
  - Explicit request: auto-rollback to prior stable if latency/error SLO breach during rollout (avoid manual intervention, reduce MTTR)
  - Needs auditability: who/what triggered rollback, timestamp, and linkable evidence (monitor snapshots)
- Observability expectations:
  - Dashboard per route/model/region + tier
  - Exportable audit log events to SIEM (they mentioned Splunk)

Security/compliance notes
- EU-only: data residency in EU region, no cross-region failover unless explicitly opted-in.
- SSO/SAML required for Console; role-based access + separation between platform admins vs app owners.
- Retention controls requested (90 days default, configurable) for logs/trace samples.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-01-16: Discovery call (Dylan + Allison). Dedicated requested due to jitter they saw on shared GPU infra elsewhere.
- 2025-01-23: Product demo (Console rollouts + health verdict screens). Customer asked, “What happens automatically when p95 blows up?”
- 2025-01-29: Technical deep dive on SLO-based rollback semantics + monitor identity (Fireflies ff-90113).
- 2025-02-04: Sent evaluation plan + capacity sizing worksheet (EU-West). Customer pushed for firm SLO numbers + acceptance criteria.
- 2025-02-11: Security questionnaire started; flagged requirements: audit logging, EU processing, retention controls.
- 2025-02-18: Working session: proposed rollout policy defaults (min traffic, warm-up window, cooldown). Customer concern: “flapping” rollbacks during low-traffic canaries.

Open questions / to confirm
- Which routes should be protected by auto-rollback (support chat only vs all inference routes)?
- Baseline comparison: customer prefers “must be worse than baseline” not absolute thresholds for every route.
- Monitor outage behavior: they prefer fail-open for serving but fail-safe for rollouts (i.e., do not advance rollout if monitors are unknown).
- Dedicated topology: single region EU-West vs EU-West + EU-North standby.

Next steps (internal)
- Allison to provide SLO query templates + recommended labels for their routes; align on p95/p99 and evaluation window sizes.
- Dylan to send pricing range for Dedicated pool + Console retention add-on; include change-management/audit features in scope.
- Loop in Rafael Mendes for on-call / runbook expectations during evaluation (what pages vs tickets, how rollback events notify).

Next steps (customer)
- Sign evaluation SOW + security addendum.
- Provide sample traffic traces / prompt distributions for sizing.
- Schedule load test window (target: week of 2025-03-10) and rollout game-day scenario walkthrough.

Notes (verbatim-ish)
- “Our agents won’t tolerate multi-second stalls; p95 is the KPI leadership tracks.”
- “We need a paper trail for every change—especially if the system auto-reverts.”
- “If the monitors are stale, I’d rather pause the rollout than guess.”
